Surveillance video released by Costa Rican authorities shows the woman accused in an incident involving a 74-year-old American citizen in Playas del Coco, a popular beach town. (Credit: Canal OIJ)

Costa Rican authorities are searching for a woman who is suspected of homicide after an American citizen was found dead in late September.

The Judicial Investigation Agency in Costa Rica, the country's equivalent of the FBI, said the agency is seeking the public's help to identify a woman suspected of homicide after an American citizen, identified as "Fleming" was found dead on Sept. 27 at a condominium near the beach.

The 74-year-old American citizen entered a condo in Playas del Coco, a seaside town in a popular tourist area on Costa Rica’s northern Pacific coast, at 4:50 p.m. on Sept. 27, according to Costa Rican authorities. The woman was allegedly seen leaving the condo without him.

Authorities then located his body, which had head injuries that were likely caused by blunt objects, according to officials.

The woman hasn't yet been identified, but authorities say she has "a fair complexion, a slender build, and black hair, and stands approximately 1.60 meters tall."

A satellite map shows Playas del Coco, a popular tourist destination on Costa Rica’s northern Pacific coast in Guanacaste province. (Maxar and Fox News)

At the time of the alleged homicide, the woman was wearing blue denim shorts, sandals and a white bra that had chain-like accessories on it. She was seen in security video released by police walking down a street with another woman.
